subject: Post-call: buying committee kickoff + security & procurement path

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — buying committee kickoff + security/procurement path

Thanks for the time this morning, Jill & Tom — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the buying committee and exec sponsor looped in: 

- Economic buyer: please confirm who will sign (we discussed Tom may be the final approver).
- Proposed attendees for kickoff: CTO (economic buyer), Head of Procurement, Security lead, Product owner, and a 1-2 person Redwood team (AM + Security/Compliance).
- Materials we’ll share ahead: 1) 10-slide sponsor briefing, 2) security checklist (SOC2 scope, data retention), 3) mutual action plan with milestones.
- Procurement asks we heard: SOC2 attestation, retention & deletion policy, and standard procurement form.

Suggested slots for a 45-min buying-committee kickoff: Jan 28 (10:00–11:00 PT) or Feb 1 (14:00–14:45 PT). If those don’t work, please propose two alternatives.

I’ll prepare a short sponsor briefing tailored to the CTO and a one-page security summary for legal/procurement. If you can confirm the procurement contact and legal reviewer we’ll route the right docs.

Attachments: none in this message — will follow with the brief and checklist.

Best,

Subject: Sponsor brief + security one-pager (for procurement)

Hi all — thanks for confirming, Jill. Per Hannah's note, attaching two artifacts we typically share ahead of a buying-committee kickoff: a concise sponsor briefing (slides) and a one-page security summary. These are designed to answer the top procurement/legal questions quickly and to arm the economic buyer with what they need for an internal briefing.

High-level items in the brief: 1) business outcomes and cost levers, 2) expected pilot timeline and success criteria, 3) high-level architecture and data flows, 4) suggested rollout and rollback guardrails.

Security one-pager covers: SOC2 status, encryption in transit & at rest, KV cache isolation options for private deployments, and our recommended data retention options.

Attaching: redwood_sponsor_brief.pdf; security_one_pager.pdf
Related links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CW-2026-011 (for internal tracking)
DocuSign placeholder (contract + SOW): https://www.docusign.com/df4x-example

If Alicia or Legal have a sprint or specific questions, point them to the security one-pager and we’ll follow up with any evidence they request (SOC2 report, encryption attestations, etc.).

Best,

Great — thanks Tom, and welcome Alicia (cc'd).

Quick answers to help your internal prep: 
- Pilot timeline: 6-week technical pilot (dev -> pilot -> evaluate) + 6-8 week optional rollout depending on success criteria.
- Latency SLO: p99 <= 180ms for our hosted instance under the 2k qps profile; we’ll provide per-route baselining in the kickoff.
- Data residency: we can host in us-west region for the pilot and provide options for Dedicated/Private if you require isolation.

Attached is a draft mutual action plan with proposed owners and dates so procurement/legal can see the milestones prior to kickoff. I’ll prepare a short TCO slide (range) and drop it in the shared Drive ahead of the meeting: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cExample
